definition_sha256_rule: sha256 of the canonical JSON of definition.json (sort_keys, separators (',', ':'), ASCII); pinned in definition.sha256

data_snapshot.status: retrospective reference, not a record of what CryptoPulse knew at the time

split.method: chronological; the first ~60% of the data span is development, the final ~40% is the untouched evaluation period
split.development_isolation: a development run receives only observations with available_at < 2026-07-22T00:00:00Z; nothing in the evaluation period is loaded, replayed or computed
split.warmup: the 31 days before 2026-04-24 provide history (24-hour references, 30-day volatility) but are not scored, so all detectors are scored on the same hours
split.sealing: evaluation-period metrics are computed only by an explicit, separately authorised run that passes this plan's sha256; without it the evaluator refuses

reference_episodes: B1 applied to the candle data of the scored period (with warm-up history); an episode belongs to a period by its first crossing; at a period end an active episode is OPEN and its matching window ends at the period end

matching.hit: an alert with the same direction as a reference episode and alert time in [onset_ts, resolution_ts] (inclusive; resolution_ts = period end if OPEN); the first such alert is the hit
matching.duplicate: any further alert matching an already-hit episode; reported separately, not counted as a hit or a false alarm
matching.false_alarm: an alert matching no reference episode; an alert of the right direction that falls within 24 h after an episode's resolution is additionally labelled LATE (still a false alarm)
matching.miss: a reference episode with no matching alert
matching.not_evaluable: for B0 only: a reference episode for which production btc_data has no reading on some UTC day in [day(first_crossing) - 1, day(resolution)]; counted as input-coverage failure, not a detector miss
matching.direction_accuracy: among alerts whose time falls inside any reference episode window, the share whose direction matches that episode

metrics: precision = hits / (hits + false_alarms), with a Wilson 95% interval
recall = hits / (hits + misses), excluding not_evaluable, with a Wilson 95% interval
misses, false alarms, false alarms per 30 scored days
detection delay from onset (alert_time - onset_ts, hours): median and 90th percentile over hits
delay from the reference first detection (alert_time - reference first_detection)
peak magnitude of hit and missed episodes
duplicate alerts and duplicates per hit
data coverage (VALID / LOW_COVERAGE / INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY hours) and, for B0, production input freshness
breakdowns: volatility regime: tercile of sigma_1h (720 h, as in B3) at the episode's first crossing; cut points = 33rd/67th percentiles of sigma_1h over all development scored hours across assets, computed in the development run and reused unchanged for evaluation
data quality: episodes with any LOW_COVERAGE hour in [onset - 24h, resolution] versus none
small_sample_rule: fewer than 20 reference episodes in a cell: the cell is labelled INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE and shows counts only; no rates are emphasised and no superiority is claimed from it
claims_rule: no detector is called better because it detects more events; precision, false alarms per 30 days, coverage and delay are always reported together; no claim is made from the development period alone
